questions.question: A single 2/0 R90 (90°C) aluminum-sheathed copper conductor is run in free air. What is its ampacity?
solution_steps: Rule (selection): free air + copper conductor → Table 1 (free-air copper). Teacher grid: Tables 1 & 2 = copper, Tables 1 & 3 = free air, so free-air copper = Table 1, NOT Table 3 (Table 3 is free-air aluminum).
Table: the conductor is a copper conductor (aluminum-SHEATHED, but the current-carrying conductor is copper), so Table 1 applies; the sheath material does not change the table.
Value: Table 1, 2/0 copper, 90°C column = 195 A.
Math: single conductor in free air, no count derate and no ambient stated → 195 A.
Result: 195 A. (Source answer 300 A / Table 3 was incorrect — wrong table for a copper conductor.)

questions.question: The insulation on the neutral conductors should have a temperature rating less than the temperature rating of the insulation on the ungrounded conductors. True or False?
questions.answer: False — the neutral (identified) conductor insulation must have a temperature rating not less than that of the ungrounded conductors.
solution_steps: Rule 4-016 2) requires the insulation of the identified (neutral) conductor to have a temperature rating not less than that of the ungrounded conductors.
Therefore the statement is False.
questions.question_fa: عایق هادی‌های neutral باید temperature rating کمتری نسبت به عایق هادی‌های ungrounded داشته باشد. درست است یا نادرست؟
questions.answer_fa: نادرست — عایق هادی neutral (identified) باید temperature rating ای کمتر از هادی‌های ungrounded نداشته باشد.

questions.question: A rigid steel conduit contains three #4 R90 copper conductors and three #1 TW75 copper conductors. What is the maximum allowable ampacity of each conductor?
solution_steps: Rule (mixed temp ratings): Rule 4-038 — conductors of different temperature ratings in the same raceway are sized on the basis of the LOWEST temperature rating present, here 75°C. So the R90 conductors are read in the 75°C column too.
Table/value: Table 2 copper at 75°C — #4 = 85 A, #1 = 130 A.
Count derate: all 6 conductors are current-carrying (Rule 4-004) → Table 5C, 4–6 conductors = 0.80.
Result: #4 = 68 A, #1 = 104 A. (Confirms the source figures; the 68 A comes from applying Rule 4-038 lowest-rating, i.e. the #4 R90 is held to its 75°C value of 85 A, not its 90°C value of 95 A.)

solution_steps: Rule (selection): raceway + copper → Table 2; base value for #4 copper at 90°C (R90) = 95 A.
Count derate: 25 current-carrying conductors → Table 5C, 25–42 conductors = 0.60.
Result: 57 A.

questions.question: An 800 A non-continuous load is supplied by paralleling single-conductor Teck cable, type RW90 copper. The cable is direct-buried and spaced 190 mm apart. What is the minimum conductor size required?
options: A) 250 kcmil (two conductors per phase in parallel, each ≈ 422 A)
B) 4/0 AWG (two conductors per phase in parallel)
C) 350 kcmil (two conductors per phase in parallel)
questions.answer: 250 kcmil (two conductors per phase in parallel, each ≈ 422 A)
solution_steps: Rule (selection): direct-buried spaced single conductors → Rule 4-004 1)d) sends you to the underground spaced configuration (Appendix D), Diagram D8 / Table D8A detail 2.
Method: two conductors per phase in parallel → each carries 800 A ÷ 2 = 400 A; pick a size whose underground ampacity ≥ 400 A.
Math: 250 kcmil at this spacing is stated to give ≈ 422 A per conductor (> 400 A) → 250 kcmil, two in parallel per phase.
NEEDS REVIEW: confirm the exact 250 kcmil ampacity for 90°C Cu, single-conductor Teck, direct-buried spaced 190 mm in Table D8A detail 2 of the 2024 code (Appendix D table not verified here).

4/0 AWG (دو هادی به ازای هر فاز به صورت parallel)

questions.question: Does an electrician need to count bonding conductors when determining the ampacities of conductors in raceways?
options: A) Yes — all conductors in the raceway are counted.
B) No — bonding conductors are not counted as current-carrying conductors.
C) Yes — but only bonding conductors larger than #6.
D) Only when more than 3 current-carrying conductors are present.
questions.answer: No — bonding conductors are not counted as current-carrying conductors.
solution_steps: Rule 4-004 6) states that bonding (and certain other non current-carrying) conductors are not counted when determining the count-derating of conductors in a raceway.
Result: No.
questions.question_fa: آیا یک برق‌کار باید هنگام تعیین ampacity هادی‌های داخل raceway، هادی‌های bonding را هم بشمارد؟
options_fa: بله — همه هادی‌های داخل raceway شمرده می‌شوند.
خیر — هادی‌های bonding به‌عنوان هادی current-carrying شمرده نمی‌شوند.
بله — اما فقط هادی‌های bonding بزرگ‌تر از #6.
فقط زمانی که بیش از 3 هادی current-carrying وجود داشته باشد.
questions.answer_fa: خیر — هادی‌های bonding به‌عنوان هادی current-carrying شمرده نمی‌شوند.

questions.question: What is the maximum ampacity of each conductor when 10 #4 R90 copper conductors are installed in a run of EMT located in a 40°C ambient temperature?
solution_steps: Rule (selection): raceway + copper → Table 2; #4 copper at 90°C (R90) = 95 A.
Count derate: 10 current-carrying conductors → Table 5C, 7–24 = 0.70.
Ambient: 40°C ambient, 90°C insulation column → Table 5A = 0.91.
Math: 95 × 0.70 × 0.91 = 60.51 A (order of the two factors does not matter).
Result: ≈ 60.51 A.

questions.question: If 35 #10 TEW (equipment wire) conductors are to be installed in one conduit, what is the ampacity of each conductor?
options: A) 16.8 A (source) — but the standard Table 5C count factor for 35 conductors is 0.60, which would give 18 A; verify
questions.answer: 16.8 A (source) — but the standard Table 5C count factor for 35 conductors is 0.60, which would give 18 A; verify
solution_steps: Rule (selection): equipment wire (TEW) ampacity → Rule 4-014, Table 12; source base for #10 TEW = 30 A.
Count derate: source applies 0.56 for 35 conductors → 30 × 0.56 = 16.8 A.
2024-method check: Table 5C for 25–42 current-carrying conductors = 0.60, which gives 30 × 0.60 = 18 A — the 0.56 factor is not a standard Table 5C value.

NEEDS REVIEW: confirm (a) the #10 TEW base ampacity in Table 12 of the 2024 code, and (b) which count-derating basis applies to equipment wire. Source figure 16.8 A vs 2024-method figure 18 A shown for a human to decide; do not silently change.

questions.question: What is the maximum ampacity of 7 conductors in a raceway located in 45°C ambient, containing four 2/0 R90 copper conductors and three 1/0 TW75 copper conductors?
solution_steps: Rule (mixed temp ratings): Rule 4-038 — different temperature ratings in one raceway are sized on the LOWEST rating present (75°C). So both the 2/0 R90 and the 1/0 TW75 are read in the 75°C column.
Table/value: Table 2 copper at 75°C — 2/0 = 175 A, 1/0 = 150 A.
Count derate: 7 current-carrying conductors → Table 5C, 7–24 = 0.70.
Ambient: 45°C, 75°C insulation column → Table 5A = 0.82.
Result: 2/0 = 100.45 A, 1/0 = 86.1 A. (Source had the two values SWAPPED — it labelled the 2/0 as 86.1 A and the 1/0 as 100.45 A; the larger conductor must have the larger ampacity.)

questions.question: A line conductor in a conduit carrying three hot conductors and a bare neutral is rated at 75°C. What should be the temperature rating of the neutral conductor?
options: B) 75°C — the neutral must have a temperature rating not less than the line conductors.
D) The neutral has no temperature-rating requirement.
questions.answer: 75°C — the neutral must have a temperature rating not less than the line conductors.
solution_steps: Rule: the identified (neutral) conductor insulation must have a temperature rating not less than that of the ungrounded (line) conductors (same principle as Rule 4-016 2)).
The line conductors are 75°C, so the neutral must be at least 75°C.
Result: 75°C.

Table/value: Table 2, #6 copper at 75°C = 65 A.
Result: 65 A (the 90°C cable rating is not usable because the 75°C termination governs).

questions.question: The ampacity of conductors of different temperature ratings installed in the same raceway shall be determined on the basis of the conductor having the .......... temperature rating.
solution_steps: Rule 4-038: when conductors of different temperature ratings share a raceway, the ampacity is determined on the basis of the conductor with the LOWEST temperature rating.
Result: Lowest (option B).
questions.question_fa: ampacity هادی‌هایی با temperature rating های متفاوت که در یک raceway مشترک نصب شده‌اند، باید بر اساس هادی با .......... temperature rating تعیین شود.

questions.question: What is the color code for phase conductors of a three-phase system?
solution_steps: Where colour-coded, the CEC 3-phase sequence is phase A = red, phase B = black, phase C = blue.
Result: Red, black, blue (option A).
questions.question_fa: کد رنگ هادی‌های فاز در یک سیستم سه‌فاز چیست؟

questions.question: Given eight current-carrying conductors in a raceway, ambient temperature of 50°C, #8 AWG 60°C copper conductor — what is the maximum allowable ampacity of the conductor?
solution_steps: Rule (selection): raceway + copper → Table 2; #8 copper at 60°C = 40 A.
Count derate: 8 current-carrying conductors → Table 5C, 7–24 = 0.70.
Ambient: 50°C, 60°C insulation column → Table 5A = 0.58.
Result: 16.24 A (option A).
questions.question_fa: با فرض هشت هادی current-carrying در یک raceway، ambient temperature برابر 50°C و هادی مسی #8 AWG با عایق 60°C — حداکثر ampacity مجاز هادی چقدر است؟

questions.question: In a room where the ambient temperature reaches 48°C, what is the minimum size TW75 copper conductor in EMT that is allowed to carry 170 A?
solution_steps: Ambient: 48°C is not a listed row → Table 5A round-up rule uses the next-higher listed temperature, 50°C. At 50°C, 75°C insulation column → 0.75.
Required base (table) ampacity = 170 A ÷ 0.75 ≈ 226.7 A.
Table: smallest 75°C copper (Table 2) with ampacity ≥ 226.7 A is #4/0 (230 A).
Result: #4/0 AWG (option D). (Either the source's ≈0.76/224 A or the round-up 0.75/226.7 A lands on #4/0.)
